## Highlights

TigerMarkView 0.11.1 gives you control over the local history it keeps and
says precisely what it stores and sends. It is the first release since 0.10.0:
0.11.0 was prepared but never published, and everything it contained is here.
The viewer, PDF export, and the `tiger-mark` command render documents exactly
as in 0.10.0, with the same active-content protections.

- **Clear Recent Files.** **File > Open Recent > Clear Recent Files** empties
  the Open Recent list at once and saves the empty list. Your documents and your
  other settings are not touched, and the session's navigation history is kept.
  The same command ends the toolbar's Open Recent list when that button is shown.
- **Uninstalling now removes TigerMarkView's local data.** An explicit uninstall
  — from **Settings > Apps**, the uninstaller, or `winget uninstall` — removes
  `%LocalAppData%\TigerMarkView` (settings, the Open Recent list, browser engine
  data) and `%TEMP%\TigerMarkView` (generated pages) for the Windows account
  that runs it. Your Markdown documents and exported PDFs are never touched.
- **A privacy statement for each version.** It describes what TigerMarkView
  stores, including the browser engine's own history of the documents it has
  shown, how long it keeps it, how to clear it, what uninstalling removes, and
  every network request: web images in documents, and how a proxy server that
  requires Windows authentication is signed in to; documents opened from a
  network share; and the installer's download of a missing Microsoft runtime.
  This release publishes the statement as its `PRIVACY.md` asset, which never
  changes, and installs the identical file in the **Docs** folder.

## Upgrading

- Upgrading keeps your settings and your Open Recent list: installing 0.11.1
  over 0.10.0, `winget upgrade`, and the first install over an Inno Setup
  installation of 0.9.0 or earlier all preserve them. Only an explicit
  uninstall removes them.
- TigerMarkView 0.10.0 and earlier left this data behind when uninstalled. If
  you uninstalled one of those versions, you can delete
  `%LocalAppData%\TigerMarkView` and `%TEMP%\TigerMarkView` yourself.

## Packaging and WinGet

- The installer is built with TigerSetup 0.14.0. Installation, the PATH option,
  Open with registration for `.md` and `.markdown`, and runtime installation
  behave as in 0.10.0.
- The WinGet manifests name this release's `PRIVACY.md` asset as the package's
  `PrivacyUrl`.
- Beside the installer, the release publishes `TigerMarkView-0.11.1-WinGet.zip`,
  the exact WinGet manifests submitted for this version, and `PRIVACY.md`.
  `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `release-artifacts.json` record the hashes of all three.

## Prerequisites and known limitations

- Windows 10 version 1809 or later, or Windows 11, x64.
- .NET Desktop Runtime 10 and the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime. They are not
  bundled; the installer checks for both and installs a missing one from the
  download the WinGet catalog lists for it.
- This build is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run; the
  published `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets you confirm the download.
- Uninstalling an all-users installation removes the data of the account that
  runs the uninstall. Other accounts keep their own folders.
- Clear the Open Recent list while no other TigerMarkView window is open;
  another open window can otherwise save its older list again.

## Install

- Download and run `TigerMarkView-0.11.1-win-x64-setup.exe` from the assets
  below. Per-user installation is the default and needs no elevation.
- `winget install ItTiger.TigerMarkView` once the package is accepted in the
  WinGet community repository.

## Privacy

TigerMarkView keeps its settings and the Open Recent list on your computer and
sends them nowhere. What it stores, how to clear it, what uninstalling removes,
and when it makes network requests are described in the
[privacy statement for this release](https://github.com/rkozlowski/TigerMarkView/releases/download/v0.11.1/PRIVACY.md).
